source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Endocrine System and Chemical Coordination
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: Oxytocin and ADH are synthesised in the hypothalamus and released from the
questions.explanation: The neurohypophysis stores and secretes hypothalamic ADH and oxytocin; it does not make them.

questions.stem: Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans and it
options: is a steroid from the adrenal cortex
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes glucose uptake and glycogen storage, reducing plasma glucose.

questions.stem: Thyroxine (T4) and tri-iodothyronine (T3) are iodinated hormones of the
questions.explanation: Follicular cells make T3/T4; C cells make calcitonin; iodine is essential for T3/T4.

questions.stem: The emergency hormones adrenaline and noradrenaline are secreted by the
questions.explanation: Medullary chromaffin cells release catecholamines during fight-or-flight.

questions.stem: Parathyroid hormone raises blood calcium mainly by stimulating
options: bone deposition and more renal Ca2+ loss
bone resorption and renal Ca2+ reabsorption
questions.explanation: PTH mobilises bone Ca2+, saves Ca2+ in the kidney and activates vitamin D.

questions.stem: Melatonin, which influences the diurnal rhythm, is secreted by the
questions.explanation: The pineal gland releases melatonin in darkness and helps set sleep–wake cycles.

questions.stem: Erythropoietin, which stimulates RBC formation, is produced mainly by the
questions.explanation: Renal erythropoietin rises when oxygen delivery to the kidney is low.

questions.stem: Peptide hormones typically act by binding receptors on the cell membrane and generating
options: a second messenger such as cAMP
a new gene inside the nucleus without any receptor
questions.explanation: Water-soluble hormones use membrane receptors and intracellular messengers; steroids enter the cell.

questions.stem: Deficiency of insulin leading to high blood sugar is called
questions.explanation: Diabetes mellitus is insulin lack or resistance; diabetes insipidus is ADH deficiency.

questions.stem: Steroid hormones such as cortisol and testosterone are chemically derived from
questions.explanation: Adrenal cortical and gonadal steroids share a cholesterol skeleton.

questions.stem: Growth hormone (somatotropin) is secreted by the
questions.explanation: Adenohypophysis secretes GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH and MSH.

questions.stem: Glucagon from pancreatic alpha cells
options: lowers blood glucose by promoting glycogenesis
raises blood glucose by promoting glycogenolysis
is identical in action to insulin
is stored in the gall bladder
questions.explanation: Glucagon is insulin's antagonist: it frees glucose from liver glycogen.

questions.stem: Calcitonin from thyroid C cells lowers plasma Ca2+, whereas PTH raises it. After a calcium-rich meal one would expect
options: more glucagon and no change in Ca2+ hormones
questions.explanation: High blood Ca2+ stimulates C cells and suppresses parathyroid secretion.

questions.stem: Releasing and inhibiting hormones reach the anterior pituitary through the
questions.explanation: A portal system carries hypothalamic peptides to adenohypophyseal cells.

questions.stem: Which pancreatic cell type secretes somatostatin?
questions.explanation: Delta cells make somatostatin, which inhibits both insulin and glucagon; acini are exocrine.

questions.stem: A dietary iodine deficiency commonly produces
options: exophthalmic goitre from excess T4 only
questions.explanation: Low iodine cuts T3/T4, TSH rises, and the thyroid enlarges (colloid goitre).

questions.stem: Aldosterone, a mineralocorticoid that saves Na+ and raises blood volume, is produced in the
options: zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex
questions.explanation: Zona glomerulosa makes aldosterone; fasciculata makes cortisol; reticularis makes androgens.

questions.stem: Hypoparathyroidism can cause tetany because of a fall in
questions.explanation: Low Ca2+ increases neuromuscular excitability, producing painful spasms.

questions.stem: Thymosins from the thymus are important for
questions.explanation: The thymus is large in children and programs cell-mediated immunity.

questions.stem: Atrial natriuretic factor is a hormone of the heart that
options: raises blood pressure by saving Na+
lowers blood pressure by promoting Na+ excretion
questions.explanation: Stretched atria release ANF, which is natriuretic and vasodilator.

questions.stem: Steroid and thyroid hormones typically act by
options: binding intracellular receptors that alter gene transcription
opening only ligand-gated Na+ channels at the NMJ
questions.explanation: Lipid-soluble hormones cross membranes and regulate DNA transcription.

questions.stem: Excess GH after epiphyseal closure produces
questions.explanation: In adults GH overgrowth thickens hands, feet and face (acromegaly); before puberty it causes gigantism.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an endocrine gland?
questions.explanation: Salivary glands are exocrine; they pour saliva through ducts, not hormones into blood.

questions.stem: Which anterior-pituitary hormone is incorrectly matched with its target?
questions.explanation: ADH is released from the posterior pituitary, not manufactured as an anterior-lobe tropic hormone.

questions.stem: Which statement about insulin and glucagon is incorrect?
options: They are peptide hormones of the islets
They have opposite effects on blood glucose
Insulin is from beta cells and glucagon from alpha cells
Both are secreted by the adrenal medulla
questions.explanation: Islet hormones are pancreatic; the medulla secretes catecholamines.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect hormone–gland–action set.
options: Calcitonin — C cells — lower plasma Ca2+
T3/T4 — parathyroid — lower plasma iodine by depositing bone
questions.explanation: T3/T4 come from thyroid follicles and control metabolism, not from parathyroids or bone deposition.
